name: Aguascalientes
note: Aguascalientes's plate is white with playful blue, yellow, purple and pink shapes, and the state name and seal across the top.

name: Baja California
note: Baja California's newest everyday plate wears the state government's guinda (maroon), white and gold colors, with a guinda band carrying the state name along the bottom.

name: Baja California Sur
note: Baja California Sur's everyday plate is a clean white plate with dark characters, the state name across the top and a barcode for quick checks.

name: Campeche
note: Campeche's new 2026 plate keeps the state's 'Campeche puro amor' spirit, with CAMPECHE across the top and a decorative band along the bottom, and adds new anti-cloning security features.

name: Chiapas
note: Chiapas's 2025 plate is a clean white design with CHIAPAS across the top and the government's 'Humanismo que transforma' logo at the bottom, packed with security features: a QR code, a hologram and an augmented-reality logo.

name: Chihuahua
note: Chihuahua's plate from the 2022 statewide swap is a plain white plate with 'CHIHUAHUA' across the top and the Mexican and Chihuahua coats of arms near the bottom, built with a reflective security film and a barcode.

name: Mexico City
note: Mexico City's everyday plate is white with black characters, a maroon 'Ciudad de México' legend beside the city and SEMOVI shields, and a QR code in the corner.

name: Coahuila
note: Coahuila's new plates from the 2025-2027 replating carry a QR code you can scan to confirm the plate is real, plus a color-shifting security pattern.

name: Colima
note: Colima's plate wears the state government's maroon, white and gold, with a little vine and two doves along the top and the state seal and name at the bottom.

name: Durango
note: Durango's plate is white with green lettering, a 'DGO.' logo up top and a bright strip of flowers along the bottom under the word DURANGO.

name: Guanajuato
note: Guanajuato's plate has blue stripes, the state shield top left, a QR code top right, and the motto 'Grandeza de México' along the bottom.

name: Guerrero
note: Guerrero's current plate carries the state government's 'Transformando Guerrero' logo and a QR code at the top, maroon-and-gold tones, and the national and state seals at the bottom.

name: Hidalgo
note: Hidalgo's plate is white and maroon with a thin gold stripe, the national and state shields along the bottom, and a QR code top right.

name: Jalisco
note: The 'Cabañas' plate is white with a row of little orange-and-blue icons up top (the Hospicio Cabañas dome, the state seal and an agave) and a QR code in the corner.

name: State of Mexico
note: The State of Mexico's current plate is white with a maroon, flower-patterned band, the state name, and the motto '¡El poder de servir!' across the top.

name: Michoacán
note: Michoacán's plate has a deep maroon band across the top with the state government seal and a QR code, and 'Michoacán – El alma de México' along the bottom.

name: Morelos
note: Morelos's newest plate uses green tones and the motto 'La tierra que nos une'.

name: Nayarit
note: Nayarit's plate is white with the state name and seal up top and a joyfully colorful band of folk-art patterns along the bottom.

name: Nuevo León
note: Nuevo León's current plate, rolled out in 2023, carries the state's 'Nuevo León' wordmark plus the state and national coats of arms.

name: Oaxaca
note: Oaxaca's colorful plate lines up figures in traditional dress from the state's eight regions along the bottom, set among maguey plants that nod to the mezcal country.

name: Puebla
note: Puebla's plate is white with 'Gobierno de Puebla — Hacer historia, Hacer futuro' across the top, plus the national shield, revolutionary figures and the state shield.

name: Querétaro
note: Querétaro's plate is white with blue bands across the top and bottom, and the state government shield and a QR code on the right side.

name: Quintana Roo
note: Quintana Roo's 2026 plate is a minimalist white design framed in maroon (guinda) with the Quintana Roo logo at the top.

name: San Luis Potosí
note: San Luis Potosí's plate is white with lime-green accents, the state name and a QR code up top, and a little skyline of landmark buildings along the bottom.

name: Sinaloa
note: Sinaloa's plate is white with 'SINALOA' and 'MÉXICO' in red along the bottom, the state coat of arms between the two words, and a QR code in the top corner.

name: Sonora
note: Sonora's new plate shows off the state's landscapes: its sierra, valleys and desert.

name: Tabasco
note: Tabasco's 2026 plate is a crisp white design with TABASCO in a maroon header at the top and a QR code for security.

name: Tamaulipas
note: Tamaulipas's 2025 plate is white with a sweeping guinda-red and gold band along the bottom, 'Tamaulipas México' up top, a QR code in the corner and the national and state coats of arms.

name: Tlaxcala
note: Tlaxcala's plate is purple and maroon with the motto 'Tlaxcala, una nueva historia', a QR code on the right, and a REPUVE chip built in.

name: Veracruz
note: Veracruz's newest plate is white with a maroon (guinda) header reading VERACRUZ, a QR code, the state seal and the 'Por amor a Veracruz' heart logo along the bottom, and it is reported to carry an electronic security chip.

name: Yucatán
note: Yucatán's 2025 plate is a simple, clean white design with a maroon (guinda) stripe and the state name at the top, with the national and state seals at the bottom.

name: Zacatecas
note: Zacatecas's plate is pale and sunny, with a desert scene of the sun rising between mountains and a QR code that stores the plate's data.
